prompt: High three-quarter aerial view of one dense city block and the streets around it, looking down at about 40 degrees from the south-west, near-isometric with very little perspective convergence, as in a detailed isometric strategy game but painted as fine concept art. The block fills the middle of the frame; its pavements, kerbs, road and tiny pedestrians and cars are legible at the bottom edge; the tallest towers rise out of the top of the frame. Every rooftop and setback terrace is lovingly detailed and seen from above: no bare flat roofs anywhere. A monorail line on slim pylons sweeps straight through the block, entering a 150 m tower at its tenth floor through a glazed station gallery and leaving on the far side; around it a cluster of stepped towers and a curved slab block. Rooftops: the station's barrel-vaulted glass canopy, a rooftop cafe under striped awnings, water towers styled as chrome spheres, a tennis court, radio masts with ringed insulators. Optimistic retro-future atomic-age metropolis, the 1950s imagining the year 2000: Streamline Moderne, Art Deco and Googie on a heroic scale, feats of engineering everywhere. Cream limestone and white enamel, seafoam-teal faience bands, coral-red fins and ribbons, brushed gold and chrome crowns, vermilion steel lattices. Warm late-morning sun, crisp shadows, a soft teal-green sky, light aerial haze on the far towers. Clean, grand, prosperous civic city; no grime. Cinematic painted concept art with photographic material realism, museum-quality composition, no text, no logos, no watermark.
